Bug_Title: ICAST: Integral value cast to double and then passed to Math.ceil (ICAST_INT_CAST_TO_DOUBLE_PASSED_TO_CEIL)
Bug_Details:
This code converts an integral value (e.g., int or long)
to a double precision
floating point number and then
passing the result to the Math.ceil() function, which rounds a double to
the next higher integer value. This operation should always be a no-op,
since converting an integer to a double should give a number with no fractional part.
It is likely that the operation that generated the value to be passed
to Math.ceil was intended to be performed using double precision
floating point arithmetic.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method where an integer value is explicitly cast to a double and then passed to Math.ceil. Since casting an integer to a double does not introduce a fractional part, passing this value to Math.ceil is unnecessary and should have no effect.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test cases call the showBug method with various integer values, including positive, zero, negative, large positive, and large negative integers. The method showBug unnecessarily casts the integer to a double and passes it to Math.ceil, which should have no effect on the result since the integer cast to double has no fractional part. The test cases assert that the result of showBug is equal to the original integer value, but the presence of the unnecessary cast triggers the bug rule ICAST.
